Metabolic Complications
Refeeding Syndrome  Refeeding syndrome is a series of dangerous electrolyte 
aberrations and fluid shifts that can occur with rapid or high dose initiation of PN, 
primarily carbohydrate.1,28,42,43,45,46 In any situation of prolonged, inadequate oral 
intake, refeeding nutrients promotes intracellular uptake of electrolytes and 
minerals for substrate metabolism that can result in decreased serum levels. This 
dramatic shift may cause generalized fatigue, lethargy, muscle weakness, cardiac

be minimized with judicious monitoring and conservative initiation of PN. Fluid 
status, weights and serum potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium levels must be 
closely monitored and repleted aggressively as needed. This syndrome can also 
occur in severely malnourished patients when EN is initiated and patients are

Glycemic Control  Untreated, refractory hyperglycemia correlates with increased 
morbidity and mortality. Close monitoring and intervention have been shown to 
decrease the risk of infection and improve patient outcomes
